title: Transformations & Symmetry
sub: Slides, flips, turns, and lines of symmetry

steps.html: Transformations
say: Today: moving shapes around. Start with the point three, two.
Flip it over the y-axis, the up-and-down line. The x changes sign: negative three, two.
Flip it over the x-axis, the sideways line. The y changes sign: three, negative two.
Turn it halfway around the center, one eighty degrees. Both signs change: negative three, negative two.

steps.html:
The rules

slide (translate)left/right changes x, up/down changes y
flip over y-axis(x, y) → (−x, y)
flip over x-axis(x, y) → (x, −y)
turn 180°(x, y) → (−x, −y)
Flip over the y-axis? The other one (x) changes sign.
say: Here are the rules.
A slide just adds or subtracts. Left and right change x. Up and down change y.
A flip over the y-axis changes the sign of x. A flip over the x-axis changes the sign of y.
A half turn changes both signs.
The trick: flip over one axis, and the other coordinate changes.

steps.html: The point (9, 1) is reflected over the y-axis. Where does it land?
say: The point nine, one is reflected over the y-axis. Where does it land?
steps.ok: Yes! Flip over the y-axis: x changes sign.
steps.okSay: Yes! Over the y-axis, x changes sign: negative nine, one.
steps.noSay: Not quite. Flipping over the y-axis changes the sign of x. Negative nine, one.

steps.html:
Distance on a grid line

(−9, −3) to (3, −3): same y, so count across
3 − (−9) = 12
say: When two points share the same y, the distance is just across.
Subtract the x's: three minus negative nine is twelve. Distance is never negative.

steps.html:
Lines of symmetry

square4rectangle2equilateral △3regular hexagon6circle∞

A regular shape with n sides has n lines of symmetry.
say: A line of symmetry folds a shape into two matching halves. A square has four, a rectangle two, an equilateral triangle three, a regular hexagon six, and a circle infinitely many.
The pattern: a regular shape with n sides has n lines of symmetry.
Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Slide: add/subtract. Left-right is x, up-down is y.

2. Flip over one axis → the OTHER coordinate changes sign.

3. Turn 180° → both signs change.

4. Regular n-sided shape → n lines of symmetry.
say: Let's review. A slide adds or subtracts. Left and right is x, up and down is y.
Flip over one axis, and the other coordinate changes sign.
A half turn changes both signs.
And a regular shape with n sides has n lines of symmetry. Great job!
